Bridgestone Anchor TS9 Track Frameset

The Bridgestone Anchor TS9 is a Japanese national team level track frameset developed for the highest demands of Track Racing.

Co-developed with the Japan Cycling Federation and supplied to the Japanese national track programme, the TS9 is a true track racing platform. It is designed to take the extreme forces produced by elite Track Cyclists and convert them into forward speed with maximum control, stability and efficiency.

Built using Bridgestone Anchor's PROFORMAT development system, the TS9 is not designed around one isolated number. It is engineered around the complete relationship between stiffness, rider input, contact patch, mass, aerodynamics and handling. For track racing, that balance matters. A frame must be stiff enough to deal with huge peak power, but still composed enough to hold its line at speed, under load and in traffic.

The TS9 uses HM-Carbon construction, an integrated seatpost structure and a T47 bottom bracket platform to create a frame that feels direct, controlled and properly race-focused. This is not a generic carbon track frame. It is a specialist Track frameset from one of Japan's most technically significant cycling manufacturers.

Performance & Engineering Highlights

- Japanese national team development: Co-developed with the Japan Cycling Federation and supplied to the Japanese national track programme.

- Built for elite track racing where stiffness, control and acceleration are essential.

- UCI registered track equipment: The TS9 is UCI registered for track racing use.

- PROFORMAT engineering: Bridgestone Anchor's development process uses simulation, prototyping and measurement to refine the complete performance system.

- Built to handle the explosive power of top-level riders, including efforts that can exceed 2000 watts.

- HM-Carbon construction: High-modulus carbon frame and fork construction designed to balance stiffness, weight and aerodynamic efficiency.

- Integrated seatpost design: Uses an ISP structure rather than a conventional seatpost to improve stiffness control and reduce unnecessary frame weight.

- T47 bottom bracket platform: A modern oversized threaded bottom bracket standard suitable for high-load track use.

- Tight rear centre: The 393 mm rear centre helps keep the bike compact, direct and responsive under acceleration.

- Track-specific geometry: Designed around velodrome racing requirements, with stable handling and direct response at race speed.

Included

- Bridgestone Anchor TS9 frame

- Dedicated chain tensioners

- Manual bag

Cockpit, Drivetrain & Build Compatibility

The Bridgestone Anchor TS9 is supplied as a high-performance track frameset and should be specified carefully around the rider, event and intended race position.

The T47 bottom bracket platform gives strong compatibility with modern high-performance track drivetrain options,

The frame uses standard axle spacing so can be used with any 100mm (Front) and 120mm (Rear) wheels.

Geometry

Why Choose the Bridgestone Anchor TS9?

If you are operating at national or international level, the TS9 offers a serious alternative to the more familiar European track framesets.

Its strength is not only in its stiffness or carbon construction, but in the way Bridgestone Anchor has approached the whole bike as a performance system. The TS9 is built around the reality of short-distance track racing: huge torque, violent acceleration, high-speed cornering, rider movement, tyre contact and the need for total confidence when the race becomes physical.

For riders looking for a genuine elite-level frameset with Japanese national team development behind it, the Bridgestone Anchor TS9 is one of the most interesting track frames currently available.

Bridgestone Anchor TS9 FAQs

Is the Bridgestone Anchor TS9 suitable for sprint and bunch events?

Yes. The TS9 track frameset is an elite level frame so it is suitable for any Track Cycling event

Is the Bridgestone Anchor TS9 UCI approved?

Yes.

Does the frameset include the fork and seat mast?

Yes. The TS9 frameset includes the HM-Carbon frame, HM-Carbon fork, dedicated Anchor TS9 seat mast, seat spacers, chain tensioners, bottom bracket adaptor and manual bag.

What bottom bracket standard does the TS9 use?

The TS9 uses a T47 bottom bracket standard and is supplied with a JIS 68 mm adaptor.

What axle spacing does the TS9 use?

The TS9 uses 100 mm front spacing and 120 mm rear spacing.

What type of seatpost does the TS9 use?

The TS9 uses an integrated seatpost design with a dedicated Anchor TS9 seat mast. This is intended to help balance stiffness, weight and frame structure for high-power sprint use.

What is PROFORMAT?

PROFORMAT is Bridgestone Anchor's development system, using simulation, prototyping and measurement to refine frame performance. For track bikes, this includes the balance between stiffness, tyre contact, mass, aerodynamics and rider control.

Is this frameset used by elite riders?

Yes. The TS9 platform was developed with the Japan Cycling Federation and supplied to the Japanese national track programme.

If you are operating at national or international level — sprinting, team sprint, keirin or pursuit — where every watt of power, every fraction of aerodynamic drag and every handling nuance matters, the T1Rs delivers. It is built to endure the extreme loads of the track, accelerate explosively out of gates and respond in corners with razor-sharp precision.

The Colnago T1Rs Track Frame is more than just a track bike—it is a performance instrument calibrated for the velodrome. If your goal is to maximise every watt, refine your handling, and ensure that your machine harmonises with your ambition, the T1Rs is a definitive choice.

Colnago T1Rs FAQs

Is the Colnago T1Rs suitable for sprint events?
Yes. The T1Rs is built around extreme stiffness, an oversized asymmetric bottom bracket and a dual-crown fork, making it ideal for explosive starts, gate efforts, match sprinting, keirin and kilo applications.

Is it also suitable for endurance and pursuit events?
Yes. Although engineered for sprint rigidity, the aerodynamic tube profiles and integrated front end also make it highly effective for individual pursuit and team pursuit when fitted with the appropriate base bar and extension setup.

Does the frameset include the fork and seatpost?

What bottom bracket standard does the T1Rs use?

What is the maximum chainring size?
The T1Rs accepts chainrings up to 72 teeth

What axle spacing does the frame use?
The fork is 65 mm (thru-axle) and the rear is 100 mm with track nuts

Is the frame UCI approved for all track events?
Yes. The T1Rs is UCI compliant for all track disciplines

Does the frame include the integrated stem?
Colnago offers different cockpit options. The frameset can be built with a 31.8 mm stem and bar combination for sprint/endurance setups or with a monocoque aero base bar for pursuit and TT applications. You can select your stem from the product menu.

How do I register my frame on the Colnago Blockchain?
Each frame comes with a unique identifier. Once you receive the frame you can register it via the Colnago Blockchain portal for authenticity verification, extended support and improved resale protection.

Yes. The T1Rs platform is designed for international-level performance and is used within elite sprint and endurance programmes preparing for World Championships, Nations Cups and Olympic competition.

Factor Hanzo Track Frameset

When one of the top track racing countries in the world requests that we design the fastest track bike in the world, the Factor HANZŌ Track is the result. In development for over 2 years, raced at the highest level on the biggest stage in the world, the HANZŌ Track pursuit racing bike is the absolute pinnacle of streamline speed.

Tailor made for the Australian national track team, the HANZŌ Track offers ultra-efficient aerodynamics while maintaining supreme rigidity for power transfer. We’ve accomplished this by maintaining the stiffness in the layup while meticulously developing the aerodynamic design. As a pure pursuit racing bike, aerodynamics and straight-line speed are the ultimate goal.

Developed in tandem with the Black Inc Zero Track wheels, the HANZŌ Track proves to be an elite tool for world record performances.

-----------------------------------------------

2027 UCI Regulations

The Factor Hanzo Track remains UCI legal under the current regulations until the new UCI rule changes come into effect on 7 September 2027. Customers who purchase a Hanzo Track frame before this date will automatically receive free-of-charge replacement forks from Factor during 2027, ensuring their frame can be updated to comply with the new UCI regulations once they are introduced.

-----------------------------------------------

Aerodynamic efficiency

The HANZŌ Track underwent a 2 year long development process to fine tune the interaction of the air flow between the bike and athlete. We converged on a radical concept that positions the legs of the fork wide to better manage the airflow around the rider's moving legs, and to produce cleaner airflow in the channel between the frame and the rider. The wide seatstays capture air off the legs and maintain the flow conditions in open channel. The cleaner air around the bike allowed us to optimize the interactive aerodynamic effect of the Black Inc Zero’s, creating a symbiotic equation for speed.

Straight-line speed and rigidity

The importance of enhancing the aerodynamics of the HANZŌ Track is finely balanced with the need to maintain the frame’s stiffness which ensures efficient power transfer under the highest loads produced by cyclists anywhere in the world. Taking advantage of our inhouse expertise in carbon-layup and developed in our own R&D facility, the frame’s material has been precisely placed throughout to ensure the highest level of rigidity. The sculpted frame uses massive chainstays to promote power efficiency while the shaping around the bottom bracket ensures smooth transition of pedaling forces through long-fiber orientation.

Black Inc ZERO Track

In collaboration with Aus Cycling, we’ve designed the Black Inc ZERO Track disc wheel to be as stiff as possible. To enhance rigidity while reducing weight, the wheels feature buttressed internal flanges, creating shear walls between the opposite wheel faces. This new technology allowed for the elimination of several stiffness plies in the overall layup. Extreme attention to detail in the alignment, cutting, and layout of the top layer of Spread Tow fibers (TexTreme) enabled us to eschew any cosmetic outer layer, further reducing weight. Results from extensive wind tunnel testing with the Aus Cycling project showed that a polished finish proved to be the most aerodynamic.

Facilitating your burst of speed

Developed in the controlled environment of a wind tunnel to excel in the controlled environment of a velodrome, the HANZŌ Track focuses on high speed aerodynamics over relatively short distances and time, illustrating the symbiotic nature of track racing where rider and equipment become one.

Swept-back seat post

The HANZŌ Track swept-back seat post acts as a key enabler in next-level drag reduction of the rider-bike system. The seat post is positioned to maximize that space between the rider's legs and the leading edge of the post, within the UCI allowable regulations.The result: reduced drag on riders legs, and cleaner flow around the seatpost area.

Sculpted front end

By reducing the frontal area, we’ve designed the narrowest possible leading edge. Optimized according to the newest UCI rules, the resulting narrow head tube dramatically reduces drag, enhancing straight-line speed essential for a pursuit track bike.

Specially developed base bar

Aerodynamically conceived considering the symbiotic relationship between rider, bike, and environment, the HANZŌ Track’s specially developed in-house one-piece base bar shape facilitates flow along the top-tub of the bike. nesting the top tube seamlessly in the stem/bar's wake.

Factor Raiden Track Frameset

Coming off the back of two massive development cycles for Factor Bikes which resulted in the new OSTRO VAM and the HANZŌ Track, the Factor RAIDEN Track takes full advantage of everything our developers learned while creating those epic bikes. The Raiden is a fusion of knowledge.

FULL BIKE PICTURED BUT THIS IS A FRAMESET NOT A FULL BIKE OFFERING

By balancing the equation between making the fastest straight-line bike in the HANZŌ Track with developing the OSTRO VAM that is more manoeuvrable and more tailored to moving in a group, the RAIDEN Track mixes the aero efficiency of a straight-line solo track bike with the ability to excel in group racing dynamics.

The RAIDEN Track is a mass start track bike with a geometry tailored to a wide cross-section of track riders. From Sprint to Madison to Omnium races, the RAIDEN Track can dominate the sprinter’s lane.

Developed after extensive research into the ideal geometry for the majority of track riders, the RAIDEN provides a race-ready position that combines responsiveness with the ability to hold an aggressive posture for the length of a track event. Factor’s hallmark handling results in a maneuverable bike that weaves through heavy traffic in bunch racing. The frame’s inherent adjustability ensures a wide range of fit options across rider sizes and track events.

Since the RAIDEN needs to be able to be effective in a variety of track disciplines, from Sprint races between two riders to a bunch of events like the Points race, it needs to be able to deliver the type of stiffness that will allow the riders to take full benefit from their power output. Every part of the frame has been developed to accommodate these high torque needs of elite and serious amateur racers. Using our in-house expertise in laying up carbon, the frame’s material has been precisely dosed throughout to ensure the highest level of rigidity. Important regions like the chainstays and seatstays have been inspired by the HANZŌ Track to facilitate power transfer while maintaining stiffness/aero balance.

Taking inspiration from the OSTRO VAM, the RAIDEN employs a front end that is aerodynamically more suited to group racing dynamics. Air flow is less predictable in bunch events where riders will be jockeying for position within the group., The initial foil shapes of the fork and headtube were inspired by shapes used in the OSTRO VAM development process. They were modified throughout the development of the RAIDEN making them deeper and better suited for flow retention of bunch racing events. The RAIDEN combines the aero efficiency of a straight-line pursuit bike like the HANZŌ Track with the efficient group dynamics of the OSTRO VAM.

Designed to complement the Aus Cycling track project and capitalize on our insights from the OSTRO VAM and HANZŌ Track development cycles, the RAIDEN is highly technologically driven while remaining especially accessible for athletes of all levels of proficiency.

Versatile position adjustment

Thanks to the rail style seatpost, the RAIDEN offers maximum versatility to adjust and dial in the saddle position for a wide variety of rider sizes and events.

Reach and stack adjustability

The standard 1 1/8” round steerer makes it easy to fit a variety of bar and stem configurations and to fine tune the rider position.

Standard T47x 68mm bottom bracket

The focus of the RAIDEN was to create accessible high performance. Every effort was made to use standardized parts for easy maintenance and service.

Ridley Arena FAST Sprint Track Frameset

The Arena Fast is developed in collaboration with the national track team of Belgium, combining their input from a rider perspective with our aero knowledge. The Arena Fast is modular framekit developed for different track disciplines and is compatible with all wheel standards on the market.

We have a long history in making the fastest bikes on every terrain for the highest level of competition: road, gravel, cyclocross and track racing. We developed the Arena TT for the World Hour Record of Victor Campenaerts in 2019. The Arena Fast is the next step in making the fastest track bike in the world.

The objective of this development was clear: create the fastest track bike on the planet. To achieve this, we pushed the UCI regulations using the 8:1 rule for tube dimensions and the use of compensation triangles. The F-Surface Plus on the frame and fork create a controlled amount of turbulence, allowing the main airflow to closely follow the tube’s shape.

We have developped the Arena Fast as a future proof modular frameset that can be used for different disciplines and is compatible with all common wheel standards on the market.

The Arena Fast can be used in the sprint and pursuit disciplines by changing the fork rake with a flip chip. There flip chips provide the option of either running a 35mm or a 45mm front rake depending on the discipline and rider preference.

The frame and fork have been designed for both traditional wheel nut and bolt-in-axles as well as modern 12mm thru-axles by using different dropout inserts and flip chips.

Ridley Arena FAST Omnium Track Frameset

Following the success of the Arena Fast, Ridley now introduces the Omnium Fast, a track bike optimized for group races on the velodrome. Building on the Arena Fast’s success, the Omnium Fast features geometry specifically tailored to the demands of omnium disciplines. It is also the new weapon of choice for omnium world champion Lindsay De Vylder.

The Omnium Fast is designed for all events in the omnium: the scratch, tempo race, elimination, and points race. These disciplines demand a unique combination of speed and agility in a peloton. In group races, where surges and unpredictable moves dictate the pace, responsiveness is critical. The Omnium Fast meets these challenges with a geometry designed for quick and confident reactions to sudden changes within the peloton.

Aerodynamically, the Omnium Fast draws on the proven efficiency of the Arena Fast (track bike) and Dean Fast Disc (time trial bike). The tube profiles take full advantage of the 2022 UCI rule changes, which allow an 8:1 length-to-width ratio compared to the previous 3:1 restriction. This enables developers to create longer, narrower tubes. The connections between the top tube, head tube, and down tube are also maximally reinforced.

Compared to the Arena Fast, the Omnium Fast has a steeper head tube angle, enhancing maneuverability and responsiveness in a peloton. The Arena Fast, in contrast, prioritizes stability and sustained speed for events requiring minimal steering. Its lower and deeper rider position accommodates a time trial handlebar for maximum aerodynamics. The head tube is shorter and features a cut-out to seamlessly integrate a time trial handlebar into the frame.

The Omnium Fast, however, employs traditional drop bars, eliminating the need for handlebar integration into the frame. Consequently, the head tube is taller. These adjustments result in an exceptionally responsive and agile bike with maximized aerodynamic efficiency.

Another shared feature with the Arena Fast is the Future Proof Dropouts, which are compatible with all current axle standards thanks to interchangeable components. Should new standards emerge, riders can easily update their dropouts to maintain compatibility.

The Arena Fast is equipped with flip chips in the fork. This allows the rider to adjust the handling of the bike to their preferences. These flip chips enable the rider to vary the fork rake and trail. When the rider places the flip chips in the forward position, the trail is shorter, and the handling becomes more responsive. With a larger trail in the rear flip chip position, the handling becomes more forgiving. These flip chips are easy to move, allowing the rider to quickly switch between different options.
